summary: Every root architect's and phase worker's session measures the six live capability rows inside Oh My Pi as it boots (after claims/register, beside the jj attribution and the Envoy role claim) and sends the report with claims/ready; the daemon normalises it (never a refusal), keeps the latest report per claim in memory and in claim_capabilities (migration 0036), logs 'capabilities: session reported' and one 'capability <name> is open: <detail>' warning per failing row at report time, renders each live row present/open/unchecked from the sessions whose claim is ready/working/idle at the report's incarnation, shows each claim's report on its view, and names open live rows on the controller's tick. Daemon API contract 18 -> 19 (register promptAgents, ready capabilities, claim view capabilities, no live status). Stage 4b gains a bun stdio MCP fixture and the full-agent and full-agent-negative checkpoints. Round 2 (the tester's fail): the github check reads the role's App login through GraphQL {viewer{login}} instead of REST GET /user, which an App installation token cannot call (403 Resource not accessible by integration); the row's detail names the login it read; the docs, AGENTS and CHANGELOG wording moved with it; the tester's red test (8a113f75) passes unmodified. Round 3 (review round 1, changes requested): Normalize puts every detail on one clean line (control characters out) and floors a failing row's empty detail to 'no detail reported' so the strict state parse never breaks; the claim view's incarnation may be empty; the ready handler hands the report hook the decision context so a disconnecting agent cannot cancel the store write; the MCP probe tears down on an abort that came while the manager was being made; a connection error's URL userinfo is redacted. Retarget round: #1843 squash-merged, so the branch is forward-merged onto main (cee5c6fc; contract 20, migration 0037), re-proved on the merged tree, and goes back through the tester and the reviewer before any READY. Round 4: the reviewer's three prose findings from the renumber (contracts CHANGELOG 19 → 20 on a wrapped line; version.go and pi-legion CHANGELOG name 8.11.0, the first release at 19, instead of 8.10.0/8.10.1 which declare 18) fixed in one commit; four round-1 threads resolved on their acceptances, the three new ones answered. Round 5: #1878 (LEGION-668) merged declaring 20, so the branch is forward-merged onto main d4534791 and renumbered to 21 in one commit (6da3ade3), re-proved on the merged tree. Round 6: the reviewer's merge-damage thread (a glued README row and two lost newlines) repaired as main wraps them, and 8.14.0 named as the release at 20, in one docs commit.
unresolved: The 'present' deployment row judged over every live session means one tree whose repository disables a tool (as full-agent-negative does deliberately) opens the row deployment-wide until that process relaunches; the plan lists this as a concern for the architect.

The pod-side proof of the github row ran against the implementer App's token redeemed through today's deployment (the grant shim); under #1843 the same gh reads the token file in GH_CONFIG_DIR — the Stage 4b run at the retargeted head proves that path.

Contract 20 is also declared by #1878 (LEGION-668) at 530e753d; the architect's rule is that whichever merges second renumbers to 21 in a forward merge (docs/solutions/legion/daemon-api-contract-collision-renumber-when-the-release-declaring-the-number-lacks-your-shapes.md).
